message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"11","text":"Therefore, since you truly are disciples of a prophet, lay aside the discord from which wrongdoing arises and eagerly undertake to do good. But if any of you doubts that what has been said will happen, let him admit it without shame, provided that he cares for his own soul, and he will be fully assured by the one who presides. But if he has believed rightly, let him confidently conduct his life as one fleeing a great fire of condemnation and entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προφήτου ἀληθῶς ὄντες μαθηταί","chosen":"since you truly are disciples of a prophet","rationale":"Takes ἀληθῶς with ὄντες and leaves the prophet unnamed, as in the Greek."},{"source_quote":"τὸ εὖ ποιεῖν ἀναδέξασθε","chosen":"undertake to do good","rationale":"The verb presents doing good as a responsibility to be taken upon oneself."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ προεστῶτος πληροφορηθήσεται","chosen":"he will be fully assured by the one who presides","rationale":"Preserves both the sense of full assurance and the nonspecific designation of the presiding leader."},{"source_quote":"θαρρῶν πολιτευέσθω","chosen":"let him confidently conduct his life","rationale":"πολιτεύομαι concerns one’s manner of life here, while θαρρῶν supplies confidence."},{"source_quote":"ἀιδίαν ἀγαθὴν θεοῦ βασιλείαν","chosen":"God’s everlasting, good kingdom","rationale":"Preserves both adjectives applied to God’s kingdom."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about discerningly and examining the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, when caught by the admonition of the one who presides, he perhaps may not go through with the sin at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses and may thereby be able, through the word of truth, to cleanse away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For when they lie uncultivated for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also ascertain who are ill in the flesh and bring them to the attention of the unaware multitude so that they may become visible, and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι","chosen":"moving about discerningly","rationale":"The adverb and the comparison to eyes indicate purposeful movement and observation, though ῥέμβομαι can otherwise suggest wandering."},{"source_quote":"πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις","chosen":"examining the actions","rationale":"The verb denotes close, potentially intrusive scrutiny, here directed toward preventing sin."},{"source_quote":"τάχα οὐ μὴ τελέσῃ τὸ ἁμάρτημα","chosen":"he perhaps may not go through with the sin at all","rationale":"τάχα marks possibility, οὐ μή gives the negation emphatic force, and τελέσῃ concerns completing the act."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας","chosen":"those who desert their posts","rationale":"Retains the military image of leaving one’s assigned position."},{"source_quote":"τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν","chosen":"to listen to the discourses","rationale":"λόγοι refers here to the spoken instruction heard at the gathering."},{"source_quote":"χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν","chosen":"lie uncultivated for a long time","rationale":"χερσεύω evokes land left barren or untilled; the unstated subject remains represented by an ambiguous “they.”"},{"source_quote":"πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"they become material for fire","rationale":"Expresses the idiom while retaining the image of becoming something on which fire acts."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας","chosen":"ill in the flesh","rationale":"Preserves the explicit distinction of bodily illness."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου γνώμῃ","chosen":"according to the judgment of the one who presides","rationale":"γνώμη denotes the presiding leader’s judgment or decision."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The rare verb προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the unstated subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται make the precise action and antecedent uncertain. The translation understands the sick as being brought to the unaware multitude’s attention and thus becoming visible, but other construals are possible.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"13","text":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize others, for the work concerns human souls. The instructor in the discourses must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning. The one who catechizes must therefore be widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless, as you yourselves will find Clement—who is to catechize after me—to be. For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item. Nevertheless, if you are of one mind, you will be able to be carried into the harbor of rest, where there is the peaceful city of a great king.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ κατηχοῦντες πρῶτον κατηχήθέντες κατηχείτωσαν","chosen":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize others","rationale":"Preserves the repeated κατηχέω word family and the requirement that instructors first receive instruction."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ψυχῆς ἀνθρώπων τὸ ἔργον","chosen":"the work concerns human souls","rationale":"Renders the singular ψυχῆς with the plural ἀνθρώπων idiomatically without narrowing the claim."},{"source_quote":"τὰς πολλὰς τῶν μανθανόντων γνώμας","chosen":"the many dispositions of those who are learning","rationale":"γνώμαι denotes the differing outlooks or dispositions of the learners in this context."},{"source_quote":"πολυμαθῆ οὖν καὶ ἀνεπίληπτον πολύπειρόν τε καὶ ἄδειλον","chosen":"widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless","rationale":"Retains all four qualifications in their source order."},{"source_quote":"Κλήμεντα μετ’ ἐμὲ κατηχεῖν μέλλοντα","chosen":"Clement—who is to catechize after me","rationale":"Identifies Clement’s prospective instructional role without adding a title."},{"source_quote":"τὸ κατ’ εἶδος λέγειν","chosen":"to discuss the matter item by item","rationale":"The phrase denotes treating the particulars individually or in detail."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τῆς ἀναπαύσεως ἐνεχθῆναι λιμένα","chosen":"to be carried into the harbor of rest","rationale":"Retains the passive nautical image that introduces the ensuing ship comparison."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"14","text":"For the whole enterprise of the church resembles a large ship carrying through a fierce storm men who are from many places and who wish to inhabit one particular city belonging to a good kingdom. Let God, then, be the master of this ship for you, and let the helmsman be likened to the Messiah, the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize, the multitude of the brothers to the passengers, the deep sea to the world, and the contrary winds to the temptations. Let the persecutions, dangers, and afflictions of every kind be likened to the towering waves; the winds blowing from land during the storms, and the gusts, to the discourses of deceivers and false prophets; the promontories and rough places to judges in positions of authority who threaten terrible things; and places between two seas and beast-infested places to those who are irrational and doubtful about the promises of the truth. Let the hypocrites be understood as likened to pirates. Nevertheless, regard sins alone as a mighty whirlpool, a Tartarean Charybdis, murderous collisions, and deadly breakups. Therefore, so that, sailing with a fair wind, you may be carried more safely into the harbor of the hoped-for city, pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὅλον τὸ πρᾶγμα τῆς ἐκκλησίας","chosen":"the whole enterprise of the church","rationale":"πρᾶγμα encompasses the church’s whole undertaking or state of affairs."},{"source_quote":"μίαν τινὰ ἀγαθῆς βασιλείας πόλιν","chosen":"one particular city belonging to a good kingdom","rationale":"Preserves μίαν τινά and the genitive relationship without identifying the city more specifically."},{"source_quote":"ὁ μὲν κυβερνήτης χριστῷ","chosen":"the helmsman be likened to the Messiah","rationale":"κυβερνήτης is the person steering the ship, while χριστός functions independently as a title."},{"source_quote":"ὁ πρωρεὺς ἐπισκόπῳ","chosen":"the bow officer to the bishop","rationale":"πρωρεύς denotes the officer or lookout associated with the ship’s prow, distinct from the helmsman."},{"source_quote":"οἱ τοίχαρχοι διακόνοις","chosen":"the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons","rationale":"τοίχαρχοι were officers associated with a ship’s sides or their rowing divisions."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοῖς κατηχοῦσιν","chosen":"the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize","rationale":"ναυστολόγοι denotes personnel who enroll or muster people for a ship."},{"source_quote":"αἱ ἀντίπνοιαι τοῖς πειρασμοῖς","chosen":"the contrary winds to the temptations","rationale":"ἀντίπνοιαι are winds blowing against the vessel."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα","chosen":"the winds blowing from land during the storms, and the gusts","rationale":"Renders the compressed nautical expression as land winds associated with storms together with blasts or gusts."},{"source_quote":"διθάλασσοι δὲ καὶ θηριώδεις τόποι","chosen":"places between two seas and beast-infested places","rationale":"Preserves both hazardous geographical images."},{"source_quote":"ταρταρέαν χάρυβδιν","chosen":"a Tartarean Charybdis","rationale":"Retains both the underworld adjective and the named mythic sea hazard."},{"source_quote":"ἐπηκόως εὔχεσθε","chosen":"pray so as to be heard","rationale":"The adverb describes prayer that gains a hearing, as the following clause confirms."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"15","text":"The passengers, then, should keep steady, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiters should remind them of the rewards. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, like a bow officer keeping watch, should relay only the helmsman’s words. The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman, should be loved, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All of them should pray to God that they may sail with a fair wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction, since they are sailing past a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time becoming discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, naked, and distressed, and again at another time becoming united, assembled, and at peace. But they should also expect to be seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing their offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—by which I mean the sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive treatment).","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐσταθείτωσαν","chosen":"should keep steady","rationale":"The verb calls for maintaining a stable position aboard the allegorical ship."},{"source_quote":"σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν","chosen":"rocking or a list to one side","rationale":"The first noun denotes shaking or rocking, while the second denotes an unequal inclination toward one side."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν","chosen":"should remind them of the rewards","rationale":"μισθοί may mean wages or rewards; “rewards” suits the catechetical application while the object of reminding remains implicit in Greek."},{"source_quote":"χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","chosen":"what each person needs","rationale":"The neuter plural participle refers to the things required by each person."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","chosen":"should relay only the helmsman’s words","rationale":"In context, the verb concerns communicating or passing on the helmsman’s words."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης","chosen":"The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman","rationale":"Retains both roles attributed to the independently titular χριστός."},{"source_quote":"γυμνητεύοντες","chosen":"naked","rationale":"The participle specifically describes going without clothing."},{"source_quote":"ἐνούμενοι, συναλιζόμενοι, ἡσυχάζοντες","chosen":"becoming united, assembled, and at peace","rationale":"Keeps the three distinct descriptions rather than collapsing them into a general improvement of circumstances."},{"source_quote":"ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες","chosen":"seasick, dizzy, and vomiting","rationale":"The three participles continue the shipboard image, and the parenthetical explanation supports the purgative sense of the last."},{"source_quote":"νοσοποιοὺς χολάς","chosen":"disease-producing bile","rationale":"Retains the physiological image in which confessed offenses are compared to harmful bile."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν","chosen":"the saving health that comes from attentive treatment","rationale":"ἐπιμέλεια is sustained care or treatment that produces the saving restoration to health."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"’ναῦται","issue":"The supplied reading has an unexplained apostrophe before ναῦται. No elision is expected at this point, so the mark appears to be a printed typographical feature rather than part of the word.","proposed_reading":"ναῦται","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"-ὰ","issue":"The supplied form is not a viable Greek word and leaves χρῄζοντα without the expected neuter plural article. The context strongly suggests a damaged or misprinted τὰ, but this remains a proposed correction to the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"τὰ","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"’ἐγρηγορὼς","issue":"The supplied reading has an unexplained apostrophe before ἐγρηγορὼς. The participle is syntactically complete without it, and no elision accounts for the mark.","proposed_reading":"ἐγρηγορὼς","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
